Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: longitudinal visit history summarization — next steps & quick asks

Elena — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

• Goal: 1) pilot a long-history summarization flow for clinicians (visit history -> concise timeline + decision points); 2) measure truncation effects and summarization fidelity across patient visit lengths.
• Primary risks you flagged: hallucination around medication changes, and summary drift when records exceed 40k tokens.
• What we propose next: run a 2-week proof-of-concept with a 200-patient shard you provide (anonymized), run our long-context eval harness, and produce: model recommendations, quantitative regression checks, and a sample prompt set tuned for your SOAP-style notes.

Attached: carepath_prompt_set_v1.json (initial prompts we discussed), plus a short pilot scope doc. Also linking the benchmark harness we used in the demo.

Immediate asks from you:
1) confirmation we can get an S3 export (anonymized) of ~200 longitudinal patients (min 6 visits/pt) by Tue 24 Aug
2) a quick list of the fields you consider non-negotiable to surface in summaries (med list, allergies, active problems)

I recommend we test two model classes during the pilot: a 32k-token open-architecture LLaMA derivative quantized to int8 for cost-sensitive throughput, and a 65k-window model (lossy-compressed KV) for highest-fidelity summaries. I sketched the initial config in the attached pilot_scope.pdf.

If that sounds right I'll pull Marissa in for the eval plan and Ben for pricing/throughput estimates.

— Soojin

Soojin — thanks for the clear summary. A few notes/questions from my side: 

1) Procurement looped in to get a sense of licensing/PO timeline; they asked for a short one-page commercial summary if we move to pilot (can Ben help with that?).
2) Regarding data: we can produce a de-identified S3 export; legal needs a short DPIA and a CSV of data mappings (we can share by Tue EOD).
3) On the model side: clinicians are most sensitive to medication list errors — if the system downgrades fidelity for very long histories, that is a showstopper. Can you quantify the expected drop in medication-extraction F1 at 40k vs 65k? Any example artifacts you can share from the demo would be helpful.

Also: curious whether Redwood's runtime can route shorter requests to cheaper variants automatically (we want cost controls during pilot).

Thanks — Elena
